You are the planning counsel for a customer-side contract review.
Map each playbook rule to likely document locations. Use only supplied paragraph and section ids.
Account for party direction and cross-references. Mark likelyAbsent only after considering the full outline.
Return one plan for every rule. Do not draft redlines.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rules:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.

ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.

ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.

ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.

ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.

ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.

ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.

ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.

ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.

ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.

ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

plans.note: Section 15 is captioned as a limitation of Garman's liability only — check for mutuality, cap size relative to fees, exclusion of consequential loss, and carve-outs for the IP indemnity (sec-13), confidentiality (sec-14) and wilful misconduct.

Section 13 is the vendor IP indemnity; confirm defence/settlement mechanics and remedies, whether it is capped by sec-15, and whether any reciprocal indemnity from Sparkling is broader than narrow misuse.
No non-compete heading; only plausible homes are the use restrictions (sec-3) or general matters (sec-20). Confirm sec-3 does not bar us from acquiring or developing competing routing software.
Watch for sole-source language in the licence grant, maintenance (sec-10) or fees (sec-11) requiring us to take support only from Garman.
Check fees (sec-11) for any pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking; an MFN running in our favour would be acceptable and not flagged.
Section 19 is directly on point: test mutuality, duration, scope (only personnel engaged on this project) and whether general advertising/unsolicited applicants are carved out.

Section 17 governs term and termination; also review the rejection option (sec-7/sec-8) and maintenance cancellation rights in sec-10 for our exit on notice and any penalty or accelerated fee on exit.
Maintenance is typically the auto-renewing element — check sec-10/sec-17 for the renewal term, the non-renewal notice window and any uncapped fee uplift in sec-11.
Governing law, venue and any arbitration clause will sit in General Matters (sec-20); confirm the law is an accepted jurisdiction and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration.
Assignment is normally in sec-20; also check the grant (sec-2) for transfer bans and sec-17 for any Garman termination right triggered by our change of control.
Confirm Garman claims no rights in Sparkling's data (relevant to sec-4 data conversion) or in any modifications/configurations we pay for; cross-check confidentiality (sec-14) and escrow (sec-16).

Section 2 grant plus sec-3 restrictions and the 'Authorized Location' style definitions in sec-1 — test affiliate and contractor use, site/CPU limits, perpetuity and any right for Garman to revoke at will.
Any inspection/verification right over our use of the software would sit in sec-3 or sec-20; check notice, frequency, business-hours limits and who bears cost.
Look for interest on late payment, cancellation charges or stipulated damages in fees (sec-11) or termination (sec-17); service credits running to us are welcome and not flagged.
Section 12 is the specifications and warranty clause; assess warranty duration from acceptance (sec-6), the repair/replace/refund remedy, and whether sec-12 disclaims all other warranties.
No insurance heading; Garman personnel attend our sites for installation and training (sec-4, sec-5, sec-9), so if nothing appears in sec-20 this is a missing-clause request.
Check fees (sec-11) and maintenance (sec-10) for minimum licence counts, committed maintenance years or non-refundable take-or-pay amounts without an exit.

Section 17 likely requires return/destruction of software on termination; verify whether it also gives us our data back and wind-down assistance, with escrow (sec-16) and survival (sec-18) as related hooks.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

paragraphs.text: 10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

This keeps the protection mutual while removing the restriction on ordinary hiring.

input.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but sets no monetary cap, so both parties remain exposed to unlimited direct damages; our position is a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality (Sections 13 and 14), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Sparkling's payment of fees due is not treated as damages. We can accept a straight 12 months' fees cap if the USD 1,000,000 floor is an issue.

ops.oldText: The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights, and Sparkling's obligation to pay fees due under this Agreement shall not be treated as damages for the purposes of this Section 15. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

paragraphs.text: 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
(a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or
(f) is disclosed to professional advisors in confidence.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").

Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

input.rationale: Section 13 contains a Vendor-side IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the licence and free of liens, and indemnifies Sparkling (and its officers and directors) for all Losses, including settlement amounts and legal fees, arising from breach of that warranty, backed by the usual infringement remedies of procuring rights, procuring an equivalent element, or replacing/modifying the Work (p0091–p0093). Section 15 expressly carves breaches of Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the indemnity is uncapped and better than the fallback's 3x-fees super-cap. No indemnity runs from Sparkling to Garman anywhere in the Agreement, so there is no one-sided or broad Customer indemnity to narrow. The clause therefore meets the fallback (and much of the preferred) position on its material terms. Noted but not flagged as deviations: no express duty to "defend" or allocate defence control, no refund remedy if the infringing element cannot be cured, the ten-calendar-day claim notice is tighter than we would prefer, and the non-IP heads (Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) are absent from the preferred position.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.

Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

input.rationale: Section 19 is a no-hire, not a non-solicit: it prohibits us (and our affiliates) from hiring "any employee of the other party" during the term plus one year, without limiting the first limb to personnel involved in the services and with no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions covering all Vendor personnel sit in walk-away territory under this rule, so the clause fails the fallback on material terms. The redline converts it to a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, running 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, consistent with the fallback and with the existing mutual bargain.

proposal.summary: Convert mutual no-hire into a narrow 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees, so we have narrowed this to a mutual non-solicitation limited to personnel directly involved in the services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with the usual carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. This keeps the protection mutual while removing the restriction on ordinary hiring.

content.text: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction exists anywhere in the agreement. Section 3's restrictions are confined to use, copying and transfer of the licensed Work; Section 19 is a mutual non-solicit of employees, not a non-compete; Section 20 and the confidentiality provisions contain nothing restricting our business.

input.quote: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
input.rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use covenant binding Sparkling, which meets the preferred position (no restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build). Section 3 ("RESTRICTIONS ON USE") is limited to conventional licence-scope restrictions on the Software and Documentation — no copying, no reverse engineering, no assignment or sublicence, and "not use the Work except as authorized herein" — none of which limits our freedom to acquire, develop or use competing routing software. Section 19 is a mutual one-year non-solicitation of employees (a separate category, and reciprocal rather than one-sided against us), and Section 20 and the confidentiality provisions in Section 14 impose no restrictive covenant; Section 14(c) in fact preserves independent development as a carve-out. Searches for "compet", "develop", "exclusiv", field-of-use and territory language returned no restriction on our business. No redline required.

content.text: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction exists anywhere in the agreement. Section 3's restrictions are confined to use, copying and transfer of the licensed Work; Section 19 is a mutual non-solicit of employees, not a non-compete; Section 20 and the confidentiality provisions contain nothing restricting our business.

input.quote: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
input.rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use covenant binding Sparkling, which meets the preferred position (no restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build). Section 3 ("RESTRICTIONS ON USE") is limited to conventional licence-scope restrictions on the Software and Documentation — no copying, no reverse engineering, no assignment or sublicence, and "not use the Work except as authorized herein" — none of which limits our freedom to acquire, develop or use competing routing software. Section 19 is a mutual one-year non-solicitation of employees (a separate category, and reciprocal rather than one-sided against us), and Section 20 and the confidentiality provisions in Section 14 impose no restrictive covenant; Section 14(c) in fact preserves independent development as a carve-out. Searches for "compet", "develop", "exclusiv", field-of-use and territory language returned no restriction on our business. No redline required.

The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.</quote>
<parameter name="rationale">Section 15 is the only liability-limiting provision in the Agreement (no "aggregate liability" language appears elsewhere; Section 13 is an IP ownership clause with no indemnity cap and Section 11 simply requires payment of Fee Schedule fees). It provides a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and mutually carves out Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap of any kind, so each party — including Sparkling — bears unlimited liability for direct damages. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees. Redline inserts the preferred mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirms fees due are not "damages"; the existing Sections 13/14 carve-out is preserved. A straight 12 months' fees cap is an acceptable fallback.

Indemnification, confidentiality (Sections 13 and 14), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Sparkling's payment of fees due is not treated as damages. We can accept a straight 12 months' fees cap if the USD 1,000,000 floor is an issue.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but sets no monetary cap, so both parties remain exposed to unlimited direct damages; our position is a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality (Sections 13 and 14), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Sparkling's payment of fees due is not treated as damages. We can accept a straight 12 months' fees cap if the USD 1,000,000 floor is an issue.

"Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights, and Sparkling's obligation to pay fees due under this Agreement shall not be treated as damages for the purposes of this Section 15. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

input.quote:
The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.</quote>
<parameter name="rationale">Section 15 is the only liability-limiting provision in the Agreement (no "aggregate liability" language appears elsewhere; Section 13 is an IP ownership clause with no indemnity cap and Section 11 simply requires payment of Fee Schedule fees). It provides a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and mutually carves out Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap of any kind, so each party — including Sparkling — bears unlimited liability for direct damages. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees. Redline inserts the preferred mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirms fees due are not "damages"; the existing Sections 13/14 carve-out is preserved. A straight 12 months' fees cap is an acceptable fallback.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (no redline).**

Section 13 does carry a genuine Vendor-side IP indemnity, despite the section body opening with an ownership statement:

- **Vendor indemnity present** (p0090): Garman warrants it owns/controls all rights necessary to grant the licence and that there are no liens or competing rights, and indemnifies and holds Sparkling (plus its officers and directors) harmless for all Losses — including settlement amounts, court/arbitration costs and reasonable legal fees — from breach of that warranty.
- **Standard infringement remedies** (p0091–p0093): procure the right, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify so the element no longer infringes without material loss of functionality.
- **Uncapped**: Section 15 states the liability limitation "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14", so the indemnity sits above the general cap — better than the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap.
- **No reciprocal exposure**: there is no Sparkling-side indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, so nothing to narrow.

Sub-elements short of the preferred wording, recorded in the rationale rather than redlined: no express "defend"/defence-control mechanics, no refund remedy where cure fails, a tight ten-calendar-day notice condition, and no non-IP heads (Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct). These are worth raising in negotiation if the file reopens, but the clause clears the fallback on its material terms.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 19, ¶p0133).**

Section 19 is drafted as a **no-hire**, not a non-solicit — it bars us and our affiliates from *hiring* "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year. The first limb reaches all of the Vendor's employees (the "directly involved" qualifier attaches only to the second, ex-employee limb), and there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions covering all Vendor personnel are walk-away territory under NOSOLICIT, so the clause fails the fallback on material terms.

The validated redline (ok:true) replaces it with a mutual non-solicit that: limits scope to personnel directly involved in the services; runs 12 months from the end of that involvement; and expressly permits hiring individuals who respond to general advertising or approach us unsolicited. This preserves the mutual protection the parties bargained for while removing the restriction on ordinary hiring.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us:

- **§3 "Restrictions on Use"** is purely licence-scope: no copying beyond backup/internal use, no reverse engineering, no assignment or sublicence, and no use of the Work "except as authorized herein." Nothing bars us from acquiring, building or licensing competing routing software.
- **§19** is a mutual, reciprocal one-year employee non-solicit — a different category, and it binds Garman equally.
- **§14 Confidentiality** contains no "no competing development" covenant; §14(c) expressly carves out independently developed information, which helps us.
- **§20 General Matters** covers only time of the essence and notices.

Targeted searches for "compet", "develop", "exclusiv", and field-of-use/territory/"engage in" phrasing surfaced nothing binding Sparkling. This sits at the **preferred** position, so no narrowing fallback is needed.

input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only liability-limiting provision in the Agreement (no "aggregate liability" language appears elsewhere; Section 13 is an IP ownership clause with no indemnity, and Section 11 merely requires payment of Fee Schedule fees). It gives a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and mutually carves out Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but contains no monetary cap at all, so each party — including Sparkling — bears unlimited liability for direct damages. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees. The redline inserts the preferred mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirms fees due are not "damages"; the existing Sections 13/14 carve-out is preserved. A straight 12 months' fees cap is an acceptable fallback.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but sets no monetary cap, so both parties remain exposed to unlimited direct damages; our position is a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality (Sections 13 and 14), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Sparkling's payment of fees due is not treated as damages. We can accept a straight 12 months' fees cap if the USD 1,000,000 floor is an issue.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Finding submitted.

**LOL-CAP — deviation (Section 15, p0105).**

- Section 15 is the only liability-limiting provision: mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, mutual "direct damages only" remedy, and a mutual carve-out for Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality) — but **no monetary cap at all**, leaving Sparkling exposed to unlimited direct damages. That fails the fallback (mutual 12 months' fees cap).
- Redline (validated ok:true) inserts the preferred mutual cap — greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable by Sparkling and USD 1,000,000 — plus an uncapped "Excluded Claims" definition (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirms Sparkling's fee obligations are not "damages". The existing Sections 13/14 carve-out sentence is preserved, and a straight 12 months' fees cap is offered as fallback.

10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.rationale: Searches for MFN-type language ("most favoured nation", "no less favourable", "favourable/favorable", "best", "price", "other customers", "third part") return nothing resembling a pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking. The fees clause (§ 11) simply requires payment per the Fee Schedule, and § 20 (General Matters) contains only time-of-essence and notice provisions. There is accordingly no obligation on Sparkling (as Customer) to offer Garman terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, which matches the preferred position of no MFN burdening the Customer. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in our favour either, but that is a commercial upside we are not required to flag under this rule.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

paragraphs.text: 10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322
17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Nothing restricts our freedom to buy from other suppliers, so no redline is needed.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Sparkling, which meets the preferred position. The licence grant in § 2 is expressly non-exclusive; the restrictions in § 3 are ordinary software use/copying limits and do not prevent Sparkling from procuring competing software, maintenance or other services from third parties; § 10 (Maintenance and Support) and § 11 (Fees) contain no requirement that Sparkling take support or updates only from Garman; and the only other "exclusive" references (exclusive remedy in § 15, non-exclusive escrow licence in § 16, non-exclusive jurisdiction in § 20(h)) are unrelated to exclusive dealing. Nothing restricts our freedom to buy from other suppliers, so no redline is needed.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no MFN obligation burdens us.

I searched the whole agreement for MFN-style language ("most favoured nation", "no less favourable", "favourable/favorable", "best", "price", "other customers", "third part") and checked both planner candidates:

- **§ 11 (Fees)** contains only a payment obligation: *"Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule..."* — no pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** covers only time-of-essence and notices.
- The only "third party" references are in the use restrictions, confidentiality, and assignment clauses — none create a matching or parity obligation.

Sparkling is therefore under no obligation to extend Garman terms no less favourable than those given to others, or to match third-party offers. That sits at the **preferred position** (no MFN on Customer), so no redline was proposed. Worth noting for commercial context only: the agreement also contains no Vendor-granted MFN in our favour, which would have been welcome but is not something this rule requires us to raise.

Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.
