input.quote: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
input.rationale: No audit, inspection or verification right binding Sparkling exists anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises" and "access" return nothing that gives Garman any right to audit our use of the Software; the use restrictions in § 3 (p0029–p0037) impose only self-executing covenants with no accompanying inspection mechanic, and § 20 General Matters contains no audit provision. The only examination right in the document (p0114, escrow materials: "Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder") runs in our favour. The complete absence of any Garman audit right is better than the playbook's preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access), and no remote or unannounced access to our systems is granted, so there is no walk-away exposure. We therefore raise nothing and deliberately do not introduce audit language, since inserting a limited audit right would create a vendor entitlement we do not currently have.

input.quote: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
input.rationale: No audit, inspection or verification right binding Sparkling exists anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises" and "access" return nothing that gives Garman any right to audit our use of the Software; the use restrictions in § 3 (p0029–p0037) impose only self-executing covenants with no accompanying inspection mechanic, and § 20 General Matters contains no audit provision. The only examination right in the document (p0114, escrow materials: "Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder") runs in our favour. The complete absence of any Garman audit right is better than the playbook's preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access), and no remote or unannounced access to our systems is granted, so there is no walk-away exposure. We therefore raise nothing and deliberately do not introduce audit language, since inserting a limited audit right would create a vendor entitlement we do not currently have.

input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 13 is the only IP ownership provision. Garman retaining ownership of the Work (Software and Documentation) and of Improvements and Modifications to it is acceptable — that is vendor platform ownership, and Sparkling holds a perpetual licence while fees are paid (17(a)) plus a perpetual escrow licence to use and change the Codes on Garman default or discontinued support (16(b)), which sits at the rule's fallback for deliverables. The material failure is the unqualified sweep of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement": that is not limited to Garman-provided items and on its face captures Sparkling's own materials, branding and the Sparkling data Garman converts under Section 4(b). There is no anywhere-in-the-document statement that Sparkling retains rights in its data (Section 14 treats data only as confidential information), so the walk-away risk of Customer IP/data passing to the Vendor is live. Redline limits the ownership sweep to Garman-provided materials and adds a Customer Data/materials ownership sentence with a no-joint-ownership confirmation; it does not disturb Garman's ownership of its Software.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 13 is the only IP ownership provision. Garman retaining ownership of the Work (Software and Documentation) and of Improvements and Modifications to it is acceptable — that is vendor platform ownership, and Sparkling holds a perpetual licence while fees are paid (17(a)) plus a perpetual escrow licence to use and change the Codes on Garman default or discontinued support (16(b)), which sits at the rule's fallback for deliverables. The material failure is the unqualified sweep of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement": that is not limited to Garman-provided items and on its face captures Sparkling's own materials, branding and the Sparkling data Garman converts under Section 4(b). There is no anywhere-in-the-document statement that Sparkling retains rights in its data (Section 14 treats data only as confidential information), so the walk-away risk of Customer IP/data passing to the Vendor is live. Redline limits the ownership sweep to Garman-provided materials and adds a Customer Data/materials ownership sentence with a no-joint-ownership confirmation; it does not disturb Garman's ownership of its Software.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

There is no "AS IS" language and no disclaimer of implied or other warranties anywhere in the Agreement, so nothing swallows the express warranty, and the §15 liability cap preserves direct damages. Minor preferred sub-elements are absent (no express professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty, and Software Repair Service is qualified by best efforts and chargeable-cause carve-outs); we note these but they do not defeat the fallback, so no redline.

input.rationale: The grant is good on two of the three material terms: our affiliates are expressly covered without any notice condition (better than the fallback), and the licence is perpetual so long as fees are paid (Section 17(a)) with no right for Garman to revoke at will — termination is limited to insolvency events and uncured material breach on 30 days' notice (Section 17(c)(7)), and on Garman's default the licence converts to a fully paid perpetual licence (p0128, p0115). You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

input.quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, cancellation charge or minimum/early-termination fee on Sparkling. Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Section 17(b) gives Sparkling an unqualified right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination payment or stipulated damages. Section 15 confines each party's remedy to direct damages and excludes indirect/consequential damages, and there is no interest-on-late-payment or stipulated-damages mechanic. Where the Agreement does address termination for Garman's default (p0128), the money flows to us (fee refund and conversion to a perpetual royalty-free licence), which is favourable and not flagged. This meets the preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Customer — so no redline is proposed.

Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Section 17(b) gives Sparkling an unqualified right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination payment or stipulated damages. Section 15 confines each party's remedy to direct damages and excludes indirect/consequential damages, and there is no interest-on-late-payment or stipulated-damages mechanic. Where the Agreement does address termination for Garman's default (p0128), the money flows to us (fee refund and conversion to a perpetual royalty-free licence), which is favourable and not flagged. This meets the preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Customer — so no redline is proposed.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Agreement contains **no audit, inspection or verification right in Garman's favour**. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "examine" and "access" surface nothing that would let Garman check our use of the Software:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use, p0029–p0037)** — the likely home for a usage-verification right — imposes only self-executing covenants (no copying, no reverse engineering, reasonable precautions) with no inspection or certification mechanic attached.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** and the notice/boilerplate paragraphs (p0134–p0147) contain no audit provision.
- The only examination right in the document, **p0114**, runs *in our favour*: "Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder" (source code escrow).

Because the rule constrains audits *against us*, the absence of any such right is better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access), and there is no unannounced-audit or remote-system-access exposure that would trigger walk-away. Accordingly I deliberately did **not** treat this as "missing" or propose limiting language — drafting in a capped audit right would hand Garman an entitlement it does not presently have.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What I checked:** Section 13 (the only ownership provision), the licence grant (§2) and use restrictions (§3), delivery/data conversion (§4), maintenance/Improvements (§10), confidentiality (§14), escrow (§16) and term (§17), plus the definitions of "Work", "Modifications" and "Improvements".
- **What is acceptable:** Garman keeping ownership of the Work, Improvements and Modifications is vendor platform ownership, and Sparkling has a perpetual licence while fees are paid (§17(a)) plus a perpetual, fully paid escrow licence to use and change the Codes on Garman default or loss of support (§16(b)) — that sits at the rule's fallback.
- **Why it still fails:** §13's ownership sweep extends to "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" without limiting that to Garman-provided items, so it captures Sparkling's materials, branding and the Sparkling data Garman converts under §4(b). Nothing in the Agreement confirms Sparkling retains rights in its own data (§14 only makes it confidential) — the walk-away risk of Customer IP/data vesting in the Vendor.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** insert "by Garman" into the ownership sweep and add a sentence confirming Sparkling owns its data and materials, with no assignment to Garman and no joint ownership — leaving Garman's Software ownership untouched.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), confidence 0.78.**

What I found in the licence grant (§2, p0028) and related clauses:

| Material term | Status |
|---|---|
| Affiliates | ✅ Covered expressly, no notice condition — better than fallback |
| Not revocable at will | ✅ Perpetual while fees paid (§17(a)); termination only for insolvency or 30-day uncured material breach (§17(c)(7)); converts to fully paid perpetual on Garman's default (p0128, p0115) |
| Contractors | ❌ Silent; §3(c) makes any sublicence subject to Garman's discretionary written consent |
| Transferable to successor | ❌ "non-transferable" grant, §3(c) assignment bar, and §20(d) consent requirement with no M&A carve-out |

Because the fallback expressly requires transferability to a successor in an M&A transaction and nothing in the document provides it, the clause fails the fallback on a material term. The redline (validated, `ok:true`) makes two minimal edits: adds "contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf" to the licensed user group in §2, and adds a mutual, consent-free successor-assignment carve-out to §20(d) that overrides §§2 and 3(c). The perpetuity and revocation points were noted as compliant rather than flagged, and the site/AS400 limits were left alone as part of the existing commercial bargain.

**Finding: compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer).

The agreement contains no Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, cancellation charge, or minimum/early-termination fee:

- **§11 (p0084)** obliges Sparkling only to pay the fees in the Fee Schedule — no stipulated damages or late-payment interest mechanic anywhere in the document.
- **§17(b) (p0118)** grants Sparkling a clean termination-for-convenience right on 90 days' notice, with no exit fee or minimum-commitment buyout.
- **§17(c) (p0128)** on termination for Garman's default runs money *toward* us (fee refund plus conversion to a perpetual fee-free licence) — favourable to our party, so not flagged.
- **§15 (p0105)** limits both parties to direct damages, with no stipulated-sum carve-out against us.

This sits at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback, so no redline was proposed.

**Finding: compliant** (WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration)

Section 12 meets the preferred position: an express conformance-to-Specifications warranty running for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and continuing while the Software stays under Maintenance Services. Remedies are real — correction during acceptance testing (§6(b)), no-charge best-efforts repair under the Software Repair Service, and full return of amounts paid if Sparkling rejects (§7–§8). Critically, there is no "AS IS" clause or disclaimer of implied/other warranties anywhere in the Agreement, so the express warranty is not swallowed, and §15 preserves recovery of direct damages.

Noted but not flagged: no express professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty, and the repair obligation is a "best efforts" standard with chargeable-cause carve-outs. These are sub-elements short of preferred wording, not material failures, so no redline was proposed.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.rationale: A text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the General Matters section (p0134-p0136, p0141-p0147, p0149) runs from time-of-essence through entire agreement with no insurance covenant. Garman is a services-touching vendor: it installs the Software at Authorized Locations and converts Sparkling's data (p0041-p0042), and delivers on-site training and implementation support (sec-5, sec-9). With no coverage at all for a vendor that accesses our data and attends our premises, this falls below even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) and into walk-away territory, so we insert a short insurance paragraph at the preferred limits as new clause 20(k), with workers' compensation and certificates on request. The fallback limits are offered in the comment.

Garman shall also maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Garman shall provide Sparkling with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage on request.

Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: 10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

content.text:
**Finding submitted: missing (insurance clause absent).**

- **Investigation:** A document-wide search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and there is no insurance heading in the section outline. I read the full General Matters block (§20 plus its continuation at p0141–p0147 and p0149) — it covers time of essence, notices, waiver, assignment, independent contractors, force majeure, severability, governing law, headings and entire agreement, but nothing on insurance.
- **Why the rule bites:** Garman is not a pure shrink-wrap licensor. It installs the Software at Authorized Locations and converts Sparkling's data (p0041–p0042), and provides on-site training and implementation support (§5, §9). That is a vendor touching both our data and our premises, so zero coverage sits in walk-away territory rather than merely below preferred.
- **Redline:** Inserted a new clause 20(k) after the entire-agreement paragraph at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). I placed it after p0149 rather than after p0147 because "(j)" is already used, so "(k)" keeps the lettering clean. The model language's "Customer Data" reference was adapted to "Sparkling's data" since this Agreement has no defined term "Customer Data" — it uses that phrasing in §4.
- The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a negotiating landing zone.

paragraphs.text: 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
(a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or
(f) is disclosed to professional advisors in confidence.
18. SURVIVAL OF CERTAIN SECTIONS

Any provisions of this Agreement that require or contemplate performance after termination are enforceable against each party notwithstanding termination. These provisions include but are not limited to Sections 13, 14, 15, 16(b), 18, 19 and 20.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: 17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;
2. GRANT OF LICENSE

Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.

Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "volume" and "non-refundable" returned no customer-side commitment language. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only), so no redline is warranted.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Sparkling data return/deletion obligations on termination in Section 17
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 17 only requires Sparkling to return Garman's Software and Codes on termination; nothing obliges Garman to help us wind down or to give back our own data. **Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Agreement contains no take-or-pay exposure for Sparkling:

- **Section 11 (p0084)** — fees are simply those set out in the Fee Schedule, with no committed minimum volume or spend.
- **Section 2 (p0028)** — additional fees arise only if Sparkling elects to use the Software outside the Authorized Locations, i.e. usage-based.
- **Section 10 (p0065)** — maintenance runs on a "renewable one-year term," not a multi-year committed maintenance tail.
- **Section 17(b) (p0118)** — Sparkling has an unconditional termination right on ninety (90) days' notice, so no spend is locked in.

Targeted searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "volume", "quantity" and "non-refundable" surfaced nothing imposing a purchase commitment or usage cap on us. This sits at the **preferred** position, so no edit is required.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Sparkling data return/deletion obligations on termination in Section 17
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 17 only requires Sparkling to return Garman's Software and Codes on termination; nothing obliges Garman to help us wind down or to give back our own data. We have added a new Section 17(d) providing up to six months of transition assistance at Garman's then-current rates, return of Sparkling's data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day data export.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (i) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) calendar days of Sparkling's request, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data in Garman's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Sparkling in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: missing** (medium severity) — no post-termination transition assistance or customer data return.

- Section 17 handles exit only in Garman's favour: Sparkling must cease use and certify destruction/return of the Software, Documentation and Codes. Nothing requires Garman to assist with migration or to return Sparkling's own data (which Garman handles under the Section 4 data conversion work), and nothing addresses deletion or certification.
- Section 8 return-of-Confidential-Information is limited to the reject-option scenario; Section 18 survival adds no exit-assistance hook. Searches for "transition" and "return" confirm no equivalent clause elsewhere.
- Because the agreement falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export), I proposed a new Section 17(d) at the preferred position — six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable data return, certified deletion thereafter — with the 90-day fallback offered in the comment. Redline validated (ok:true) and finding submitted.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Sparkling)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Garman Software License and Maintenance Agreement
**Status:** Findings verified against the document as supplied; verification step skipped on all items.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. On balance the paper is favourable to us in several respects: the licence is perpetual while fees are paid, we hold a 90-day termination-for-convenience right with no exit fee, there is no vendor audit right, no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN and no liquidated damages payable by us. The warranty package in § 12 and the Vendor IP indemnity in § 13 (uncapped by virtue of the § 15 carve-out) both meet or exceed our fallback positions.

Six items require action. Three are critical or high-severity structural gaps: (i) § 13 sweeps ownership of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to" the Agreement, which on its face captures our own materials, branding and the data Garman converts under § 4(b), with no statement anywhere that we retain rights in our data; (ii) § 15 contains **no monetary cap at all**, so we bear unlimited liability for direct damages; and (iii) § 20(d), read with § 3(c), is a flat consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard. In addition, the licence is non-transferable and silent on contractors, § 19 is a full no-hire rather than a non-solicit, there is no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, and there is no vendor insurance covenant.

Governing law (§ 20(h), Nova Scotia law, non-exclusive venue) sits outside our accepted list on a literal reading but runs in our favour — it is our home jurisdiction, the vendor's is Saskatchewan, and there is no arbitration or foreign seat. We flag it for business confirmation only and recommend accepting it as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Unqualified ownership sweep of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" is not limited to Garman-provided items and captures our materials, branding and converted data; no statement that we retain rights in our data (§ 14 treats data only as confidential information). |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap anywhere; each party, including us, bears unlimited liability for direct damages. Fails the fallback (mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees). Mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the §§ 13/14 carve-outs are acceptable and preserved. |
| 3 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Vendor-side IP indemnity covering Losses, settlements and legal fees, with procure/replace/modify remedies; uncapped via the § 15 carve-out, so better than the fallback 3x-fees super-cap. No Customer-side indemnity anywhere. No express "defend" duty, no refund remedy and a 10-day claim notice — noted, not flagged. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(d); § 3(c)) | Flat consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard; fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so nothing to delete there. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of License | Affiliate coverage and perpetuity are good (better than fallback on affiliates). Fails the fallback on transferability: licence is "non-transferable", § 3(c) bars sublicence/assignment absent consent, § 20(d) has no successor carve-out; contractors acting on our behalf are unaddressed. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | Licence expressly non-exclusive; no sole-supplier obligation; §§ 10–11 do not require us to take support only from Garman. Meets preferred position. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, cancellation charge or early-termination fee on us; § 17(b) convenience right carries no termination payment. Refund/perpetual-licence mechanic on Garman default runs in our favour. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | § 3 is limited to conventional licence-scope restrictions; no field-of-use or territory covenant; § 14(c) preserves independent development. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination | Unconditional customer right on 90 days' notice, no fee; Garman has no convenience right. Sits at the fallback (60–90 days) rather than the preferred 30 days. Silence on pro-rata refund of prepaid maintenance noted only. |
| 10 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | **Deviation** | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Drafted as a no-hire covering "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year, with no limitation to personnel involved in the services and no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs. No-hire provisions covering all personnel are walk-away territory. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17 runs one way only (we cease use and return/destroy Garman materials). No wind-down assistance, no return of our data (which Garman handles under § 4) and no certified deletion. Fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Needs review (business call)** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive venue is outside the accepted list, but is our home jurisdiction (vendor is in Saskatchewan), with no arbitration and no foreign seat. Benefits us; we recommend acceptance absent a portfolio-consistency instruction. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No audit, inspection or verification right binding us anywhere; better than preferred. The only examination right (escrow materials) runs in our favour. We deliberately do not introduce audit language. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking; § 11 simply requires payment per the Fee Schedule. |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap; maintenance runs in renewable one-year terms; 90-day exit right preserved. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 10 Maintenance and Support | Maintenance is a "renewable one-year term" (renewal by agreement), no auto-renewal and no non-renewal notice hurdle; licence perpetual while fees are paid. No renewal reminder and no uplift cap — commercial ask only. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Conformance warranty for the acceptance period plus one year and for so long as Maintenance Services continue; real remedies (correction, repair, full refund on rejection); no "AS IS" and no implied-warranty disclaimer. Absence of services/compliance/no-malicious-code warranties noted only. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Page 10 (General Matters) | No insurance covenant anywhere, for a vendor that installs at Authorized Locations, converts our data and delivers on-site training. Falls below the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) and into walk-away territory. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the findings that our playbook treats as walk-away territory rather than ordinary negotiation. We should not sign as drafted without movement on each.

1. **Customer IP and data ownership (§ 13).** The unqualified ownership sweep of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" is not confined to Garman-provided items and, with no retained-rights statement anywhere, leaves live the risk that our data, materials and branding pass to the Vendor.
2. **Unlimited liability (§ 15).** No cap of any kind; our own exposure for direct damages is unlimited, against a fallback requiring a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees.
3. **Blanket assignment prohibition (§ 20(d), with § 3(c)).** Consent required for any assignment, with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard — a blanket bar on customer assignment.
4. **No-hire covenant (§ 19).** A term-plus-one-year prohibition on hiring any employee of the other party, unlimited by involvement in the services and without advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
5. **No vendor insurance.** No coverage at all for a vendor that accesses our data and attends our premises.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on the six actionable items:
   - § 13 — limit the ownership sweep to Garman-provided materials and add a Customer Data/materials ownership sentence with a no-joint-ownership confirmation, leaving Garman's ownership of its Software undisturbed.
   - § 15 — insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirmation that fees due are not "damages"; preserve the existing §§ 13/14 carve-out. Fallback: a straight 12 months' fees cap.
   - § 20(d) and § 3(c) — add an affiliate/successor carve-out for us on written notice, a not-unreasonably-withheld standard for other assignments, and a bar on Garman assigning to a competitor of ours; the § 3(c) edit is a conforming cross-reference.
   - § 2 — extend the licensed user group to contractors acting on our behalf and permit consent-free assignment of the licence to a successor in a merger or sale of the business.
   - § 19 — convert the no-hire into a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, running from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
   - New § 17(d) — six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return of our data in machine-readable form, certified deletion thereafter; flag the 90-day fallback in the comment.
   - New § 20(k) — insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' compensation) at preferred limits, certificates on request; offer the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in the comment.
2. **Obtain a business decision on governing law.** Absent a specific instruction that the deal team wants a US-law contract for portfolio consistency, we recommend accepting § 20(h) as drafted. If instructed otherwise, the minimal edit is to substitute New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the rest of § 20(h) intact.
3. **Two commercial asks (not legal redlines).** Confirm with procurement whether the Fee Schedule permits Garman to reset maintenance fees on renewal; if so, request a CPI/3% uplift cap. Separately, consider asking for a pro-rata refund of prepaid maintenance on a convenience termination, which § 17 does not address.
4. **Drafting nits to raise only if the document is otherwise reopening.** Clarify "renewable" in § 10 as "renewable by mutual written agreement"; consider adding an express duty to "defend" and a refund remedy in § 13, and services/compliance-with-laws/no-malicious-code warranties in § 12. None of these defeats a fallback and none is being redlined.
5. **Do not introduce** audit language into the Agreement. Garman currently has no audit right at all, and inserting a limited one would create a vendor entitlement we do not presently face."}
